questions.question: Explain why SMMEs (sole traders, partnerships and small companies) are important for job creation in South Africa, and name three obstacles they face.
questions.expected_answer: There are very many of them; they are cheap and easy to start, so unemployed people can create jobs for themselves and others; they are often labour-intensive, creating more jobs per rand of capital; they operate in townships, villages and small towns; they grow into bigger firms (the NDP expected about 90% of new jobs from small and expanding firms). Obstacles: limited capital and difficulty getting loans; lack of business skills; crime; unreliable electricity/infrastructure; cost of regulation; high failure rate.

questions.question: Compare the contribution of a small sole trader and a large public company to job creation.
questions.expected_answer: Sole trader: few jobs, created quickly and cheaply, often labour-intensive and for people with few other options, close to home; but insecure, often low paid, without benefits, and lost if the owner fails or dies (no continuity). Public company: thousands of direct jobs and many indirect jobs at suppliers and local shops; more secure, better paid, with benefits and training; continuity; but often capital-intensive and may retrench many workers at once.

questions.question: Explain what sustainable use of natural resources means and give one sustainable practice each for a farm, a factory and a mine.
questions.expected_answer: Using natural resources to meet present needs without reducing the ability of future generations to meet theirs: using renewable resources no faster than they are replaced, using non-renewable resources efficiently, reducing waste and pollution and restoring land. Farm: drip irrigation, crop rotation, careful use of fertiliser and pesticides. Factory: cleaner/more efficient kilns or energy, recycling waste, rehabilitating clay pits. Mine: rehabilitating land (with funds set aside), treating water, reducing energy use, environmental impact assessment.
